title: → run sub-skill resolution — a fresh agent given a v2-composed CLAUDE.md must look up the name in docs/sub-skill-catalog.md, read the catalog's recorded source file, and execute it; unresolved or missing-file references are surfaced as errors, never silently skipped (PRD-D / Story D7)

questions.question:
Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md (especially §4.5) and docs/sub-skill-catalog.md. Your composed CLAUDE.md contains exactly this line in the Instructions section:

  → run sub-skill: boot-bootstrap

Describe what you do, in order. Your answer MUST name (a) which file you consult to discover the source path, (b) what specific information the file gives you about boot-bootstrap, (c) the relative path you end up reading, and (d) what you do with the content of that file once you read it.
questions.expected: (a) Consult docs/sub-skill-catalog.md — that is the authoritative gate per §4.5 step 2. (b) The catalog table row for `boot-bootstrap` records its recorded source path. (c) The resolved relative path is references/sub-skills/common/boot-bootstrap.md (the canonical authoring location under references/sub-skills/; today there is no .claude/skills/ install per §4.5.1 Gap callout). (d) Read that file and execute its instructions in-context — §4.5.1 explicitly states: 'An agent encountering → run sub-skill: pipeline-sentinel resolves it by reading the catalog-recorded source file and executing its instructions in-context — not by invoking the Skill tool.' The same resolution mechanism applies to every → run sub-skill: <name> reference. Critically: the reference is NOT an inlined body; the body lives at the catalog-recorded source path and must be fetched at runtime.

questions.question:
Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5 and docs/sub-skill-catalog.md. Your composed CLAUDE.md contains:

  → run sub-skill: phantom-skill-that-does-not-exist

The name `phantom-skill-that-does-not-exist` has NO matching row in docs/sub-skill-catalog.md. What is the correct behaviour and why is silently skipping forbidden?
questions.expected: The reference is an error and the agent must surface it — never silently skip. Per §4.5 step 2: 'Every reference must have a matching catalog entry. Sub-skills not indexed in the catalog are not valid references, even if a same-named file exists on disk.' And §4.5 step 3: 'Reject if any reference fails either check above (no catalog entry OR catalog entry's source path missing on disk): abort with a diagnostic naming the offending step ID and unresolved sub-skill name. No partial output is written.' At compose time the catalog gate aborts; at runtime, if such a reference somehow reaches an agent, the agent must announce the unresolved name (which step it came from, which sub-skill failed lookup) rather than continue as if the step had no body. Silent fall-through would mean a step that was supposed to do work simply does nothing, with no audit trail.

questions.question:
Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5. Your composed CLAUDE.md contains:

  → run sub-skill: cycle-runner

The name `cycle-runner` HAS a catalog row pointing at references/sub-skills/common/cycle-runner.md, but that file does not exist on disk. Distinguish this failure mode from the no-catalog-row case and state the correct behaviour.
questions.expected: This is the second of the two distinct gate failures named in §4.5 step 2: 'The catalog's recorded source path for that entry must point at an existing file.' §4.5 step 3 rejects this case for the same reason as no-catalog-row: 'no catalog entry OR catalog entry's source path missing on disk: abort with a diagnostic naming the offending step ID and unresolved sub-skill name. No partial output is written.' The diagnostic distinction matters because the PM-side fix is different: a missing catalog row gets added or renamed in docs/sub-skill-catalog.md; a missing source file gets restored at the catalog's recorded path (or the catalog row updated to the new location). Either way, the agent surfaces the failure — never proceeds with the step body left unresolved.

questions.question:
Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5 and §4.1. Your composed CLAUDE.md's Instructions section contains, in order:

  → run sub-skill: boot-bootstrap
  → run sub-skill: cycle-runner
  → run sub-skill: vault-remember

All three resolve cleanly in the catalog. Walk through what you do, paying explicit attention to ORDER and whether you skip any.
questions.expected: Resolve all three references in source order — top to bottom — by performing the §4.5 resolution for each name (catalog lookup → catalog-recorded source path → read file → execute its instructions in-context), in the same order they appear in the Instructions section. Do not skip any: every reference is a step in the orchestration sequence per §4.1's slot+ordinal layout, and dropping one would leave a cycle step unexecuted. Do not reorder: the source order IS the execution order; the orchestrator deliberately placed boot-bootstrap before cycle-runner before vault-remember so the boot routine runs before the cycle runner runs before the vault write. The composed CLAUDE.md never inlines the bodies (per §4.1 'instructions slot is emitted as sub-skill references, not inlined sub-skill bodies'), so the three reads are runtime work, not compose-time work.

questions.question: Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.1 (specifically the paragraph beginning 'compose.py reads frontmatter from every L1-L3 file'). Your composed CLAUDE.md's Instructions section has step headers and `→ run sub-skill: <name>` lines but NO inlined sub-skill bodies. A teammate asks: 'Doesn't compose inline the sub-skill bodies into the composed CLAUDE.md so the agent has everything it needs?' Explain the correct architectural invariant, citing the specific sentence that locks it down.
questions.expected: No — compose intentionally does NOT inline sub-skill bodies into the composed CLAUDE.md. §4.1 states explicitly: 'the instructions slot is emitted as sub-skill references, not inlined sub-skill bodies, per §4.1 step 4. Concretely: the source files in the instructions slot already contain the reference text directly (e.g., → run sub-skill: pipeline-sentinel), and compose emits that text verbatim without transformation — there is no compile step that converts inlined sub-skill bodies into references.' This 'thin-orchestration invariant' (referenced in §4.4 and §6.3) is intentional: the composed CLAUDE.md stays compact and authoritative for the orchestration order; each sub-skill body lives at exactly one place (the catalog-recorded source path) so updating it does not require recomposing every role. The agent fetches sub-skill bodies on demand by reading the catalog-recorded source path at runtime.

questions.question:
Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5 step 2 carefully. Suppose a file exists at references/sub-skills/common/my-rogue-sub-skill.md (on disk, well-formed, with frontmatter) but there is NO row for `my-rogue-sub-skill` in docs/sub-skill-catalog.md. Your composed CLAUDE.md happens to contain:

  → run sub-skill: my-rogue-sub-skill

Is the reference valid? Quote the specific sentence that decides the answer.
questions.expected: The reference is INVALID. §4.5 step 2 contains the load-bearing sentence: 'Every reference must have a matching catalog entry. Sub-skills not indexed in the catalog are not valid references, even if a same-named file exists on disk.' The catalog — not the filesystem — is the authoritative gate. A rogue source file that happens to sit at the canonical path is not enough; without a catalog row the reference fails the gate and compose aborts (or, if such a reference reaches an agent at runtime, the agent surfaces the failure). The corollary: PM-side fixes for an unresolved reference begin by editing the catalog, not by adding a file to the source tree.

questions.question: Read docs/COMPOSE-ARCHITECTURE.md §4.5 step 4. The composed Instructions section contains four sub-skill references, of which three are unresolved (no catalog row) and one resolves cleanly. The catalog drift check / catalog gate aborts compose. What does the abort diagnostic contain — just the first unresolved name, or all of them — and why does the architecture insist on this behaviour?
questions.expected: The diagnostic reports ALL unresolved references, not just the first. §4.5 step 4 states: 'compose emits a warning listing the drifted entries (catalog rows without a source file and/or source files without a catalog row), then aborts with a diagnostic. The warning before abort is intentional — it gives the operator a complete drift report rather than just the first unresolved name.' Reporting all at once means the operator can fix the catalog or restore the missing source files in one pass, rather than running compose, fixing one, re-running, fixing the next, and so on. The same principle applies to the resolution gate in step 3 (one diagnostic listing every unresolved/missing-file reference). This also matches PRD-D D3/D4's implementation: the catalog gate's GateResult.format() and the catalog drift scan's DriftReport.format() each render the full multi-issue report in stderr.
